subtopics.title: Two Accounts, One Total — Defining Mechanical Energy

questions.question: Mechanical energy is defined as:
options: The sum of the gravitational potential energy and the kinetic energy
The difference between potential and kinetic energy

questions.question: A 2 kg ball is held at rest 20 m above the ground. Taking the ground as reference, its mechanical energy is:
Energy quantities such as $E_p$, $E_k$ and $E_M$ are:

subtopics.title: The Law of Conservation and Its Mechanical Special Case

questions.question: The law of conservation of energy states that energy:
options: Cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or converted

questions.question: Mechanical energy is conserved only when:
options: No friction or air resistance acts on the object

questions.question: The principle of conservation of mechanical energy is written as:
A ball falls through air with noticeable air resistance. Which statement is correct?
options: Both total and mechanical energy are conserved
Total energy is conserved but mechanical energy decreases

subtopics.title: The Falling Ball — Working the Energy Ledger

questions.question: The 2 kg ball, dropped from 20 m, passes the 10 m mark. Its kinetic energy there is:
At the 10 m mark, the ball's speed is found from $\frac{1}{2}(2)v^2 = 196$, giving:
Just before the ground, all 392 J is kinetic. The ball's speed is:
Setting $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh$ and cancelling the mass shows that the landing speed of a dropped object:
options: Does not depend on its mass
Depends on the reference point chosen

subtopics.title: Reference Points, Leaks and the Habits That Bank the Marks

questions.question: The value of g used in CAPS energy calculations is:
A learner measures the first height from the ground and the second from a balcony. The error is:
A question states the surface is rough. Mechanical energy along the motion:
options: Is not conserved — some is transferred to heat

questions.question: The kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 14 m/s is:
In the wallet picture, the height pocket and speed pocket stand for:
options: Gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy

questions.question: The wallet is sealed — the total cannot change — as long as:
options: Nothing rubs: no friction and no air resistance
The object moves in a straight line

questions.question: Choosing where height counts as zero is:
options: Your choice, but it must stay the same for the whole problem
Fixed by the mass of the object

questions.question: At the top of the roof the wallet reads 392 J plus 0 J. Halfway down it reads:
A speed pocket holding 196 J for the 2 kg ball means a speed of:
The bank-statement check — saying 392 plus 0, then 196 plus 196, then 0 plus 392 — is useful because:
options: The two pockets must always add to the sealed total, so a slip shows up immediately
It replaces the need for units
It proves the mass is 2 kg
It shows energy is a vector

questions.question: A 5 kg ball and a 2 kg ball are dropped from the same roof with no air resistance. They land:
options: With the heavy ball much faster
At the same speed, because the mass cancels
At speeds proportional to their masses

questions.question: When friction acts, the mechanical energy that leaves the wallet:
options: Becomes heat and a little sound — total energy is still conserved

questions.question: Which phrase in an exam question is your licence to use conservation of mechanical energy?
Touching a bicycle's brake rim after braking, you feel warmth. This is evidence that:
options: Kinetic energy disappeared from the universe
The lost mechanical energy was transferred to heat
